metadata.remarks: The obligation set that applies from 2 August 2026 to providers and deployers of the AI systems covered by Article 50, irrespective of risk classification. Following Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, which deferred the stand-alone Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027, Article 50 is the principal substantive obligation that lands on 2 August 2026 — so this, not the high-risk profile, is the near-term readiness target. Four distinct duties are in scope and are commonly conflated: informing natural persons that they are interacting with an AI system (Article 50(1), provider); machine-readable marking of synthetic audio, image, video and text output (Article 50(2), provider); informing persons exposed to emotion-recognition or biometric-categorisation systems (Article 50(3), deployer); and disclosing deep-fake and public-interest text content (Article 50(4), deployer). Assess each separately. Generative systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 have until 2 December 2026 to satisfy the Article 50(2) marking duty (Article 111(4) as inserted by the Omnibus); systems placed on the market on or after that date do not.
